## Big Data Econometrics - Week 3 

# Exercise 4.3

We will be using factor models to see if we could have predicted large (recent) inflation.
We will use the monthly FRED data to conduct the analysis.

First, we have to import and retrieve the necessary data from the dataset using the given "Exercise_4_3_preparation.R" file.

```{r}
# import relevant packages
library(bootUR)
library(zoo)
library(dfms)
set.seed(333)

# use the given .r file to get the data
source("Exercise_4_3_preparation.R")

```

We can now start with the processing.

```{r}
# so we will take the cpi from the transformed data
infl <- as.numeric(fred_final$CPIAUCSL)
plot(as.Date(dates), infl, type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "CPI inflation (monthly)")

# initialise the horizons to use
h1 <- 1
h3 <- 3
h6 <- 6
window <- 240 # 20 years

```

Now we need to do the rolling window predictions.

```{r}
# initialise all necessary aspects for the rolling window
dates <- index(fred_final)
x_all <- as.matrix(fred_final[, colnames(fred_final) != "CPIAUCSL"])


# set the training range
train_end_date <- as.yearmon("Dec 2014")
train_idx      <- which(dates <= train_end_date)

# set the training dates
xtrain <- x_all[train_idx,]


ic <- ICr(xtrain, max.r = 20)
print(ic)       # shows the criteria for each number of factors
plot(ic)        # scree plot / IC curves
ic$r.star       # optimal number of factors according to IC1, IC2, IC3

r <- ic$r.star[1]   # use IC1 (check the printout; pick whichever you prefer)
r
```
